note: Diagnostico quirurgico de timeGridCatalogCache (P1 de 14I.1). No se cambio codigo productivo. Hallazgo principal: un bug de coercion de zod (independiente de la cache en si) hace que includeDetails=false nunca funcione desde el cliente, nunca detectado en 6 auditorias previas (14A/9A/14I.1/14I.3/14I.6/14I.7).

relatedStages.14A: docs/decisions/PERFORMANCE_AUDIT_14A.md (primera mencion, 'Severidad Alto por ser la unica excepcion')

callSitesDescription: silent re-sync after saving an hour entry or manual breakdown

key: none — single global entry, no user/role/query/date scope

cachedData.noveltyTypes: all NoveltyType rows with status=ACTIVO (up to 500), include finnegansLinks
cachedData.hourConcepts: all HourConcept rows with status=ACTIVO (up to 100)

newBugFound.description: employees.schemas.ts:198 declares includeDetails: z.coerce.boolean().default(true). z.coerce.boolean() applies JS Boolean(value); a querystring value always arrives as a string, and Boolean("false") is true (any non-empty string is truthy). So ?includeDetails=false is coerced to true, the same as omitting it or passing true.
newBugFound.reproduction: node -e "const {z}=require('zod'); console.log(z.object({includeDetails:z.coerce.boolean().default(true)}).parse({includeDetails:'false'}))" -> { includeDetails: true } (verified against the actually installed zod@3.25.76)
newBugFound.consequence: The only real caller (EmployeeHoursPage.tsx) always intends includeDetails=false but the backend always executes the heavy branch (period novelties fetch + getTimeGridCatalogs()) on every page load AND every post-save silent resync.
newBugFound.mitigatingFactor: The frontend discards the 3 fields gated by includeDetails (novelties, noveltyTypes, hourConcepts) unconditionally — it always overwrites them from separate, correctly-cached-and-invalidated calls (noveltyApiService.getAll, noveltyTypeApiService.getAll) and builds hour-concept rows from grid.employee.hourConcepts + grid.normalConcept, never from the embedded catalog. So the functional risk today is nil.
newBugFound.realCost: novelty.findMany (up to 200 rows, rich include) runs uncached on every load/save of the hours page for that employee/period — wasted work, not bounded by any TTL. getTimeGridCatalogs() is global and TTL-bounded (120s), so its marginal cost is low but still runs unnecessarily on the first miss of every 120s window app-wide.

risk.functional: none today — embedded catalog fields (novelties/noveltyTypes/hourConcepts) are read by the API response but never consumed by the only frontend caller; if the invalidation gap alone existed without the includeDetails bug, worst case would be up to 120s of stale catalog data shown nowhere
risk.securityScope: none — no user/role/scope dimension in the cached data (active NoveltyType/HourConcept catalog, same for all 3 roles that can reach the endpoint), no PII
risk.performance: real and currently active — due to the includeDetails bug, an uncached novelty.findMany (up to 200 rows) runs on every hours-page load and every post-save silent resync for that employee/period, doing work whose result is always discarded; getTimeGridCatalogs() itself is cheap (TTL-bounded, global) but also runs unnecessarily

existing.covers: PII redaction of getTimeGrid response, mocks employeesRepository.findTimeGrid entirely — does not exercise getTimeGridCatalogs()/timeGridCatalogCache or the real zod schema
response mapping with includeDetails:false passed by the client, mocks the HTTP response directly — does not exercise the real employeeTimeGridQuerySchema or the coercion bug

missing: hit/miss/TTL/scope test for timeGridCatalogCache itself (same gap 14I.1 already named)
a test asserting what employeeTimeGridQuerySchema.parse({includeDetails: 'false'}) actually returns — would have caught the coercion bug

measurement.method: read-only, isolated execution of the real installed zod schema logic (node -e), no HTTP request, no DB write, no test data created
measurement.result: includeDetails='false' (string, as Express delivers it) -> coerced to true; includeDetails omitted -> true (schema default); includeDetails='true' -> true
measurement.realVolumeQuery: not run — out of scope, this etapa's evidence is about query-param coercion logic, not data volume

recommendation.immediate: No fix applied in this stage (diagnostic-only, as instructed). Two candidate actions identified, both require explicit user authorization before touching production:
recommendation.candidateA_higherValue: Fix employees.schemas.ts:198 (includeDetails: z.coerce.boolean().default(true)) to correctly parse the 'false' string from a querystring — e.g. z.enum(['true','false']).default('true').transform(v => v === 'true'). Removes real, recurring wasted work (uncached per-request novelty.findMany). No observable contract change (same response shape; the 3 gated fields just come back empty instead of unused-but-populated when the caller truly wants includeDetails=false).
recommendation.candidateB_lowerPriorityGivenFindings: Add invalidation to timeGridCatalogCache from noveltyTypesService.create/update and hourConceptsService.create/update/remove — closes 14I.1's original P1, but with near-zero real impact today since nothing consumes the cached data. Valid alternative: explicitly document why it's not needed (closed-set criterion, same as 14G.8), given today's lack of a real consumer.

recommendationFor14I9: If no fix is authorized soon: pick up another P1/P2 from the 14I.1 inventory (StrictMode duplicate of GET /employees/:id/time-grid x3, named by 14G.9, never closed; or the finnegansLinks/timeEntryInclude over-fetch P2 items from 14I.1 §8)

If candidateA is authorized: scope 14I.9 to exactly that fix (1 line in employees.schemas.ts) + new tests pinning includeDetails=false really taking the light branch + full backend validations + before/after measurement if the environment allows it
The StrictMode duplicate x3 of this same endpoint (14G.9, never closed) is a natural companion to bundle with the includeDetails fix, since both live in the same caller (EmployeeHoursPage.tsx)
